limitations: Small sample size, primarily Korean undergraduate students, limiting generalizability to broader populations (cultural background, prior VR experience, personal preferences may influence spatial perception and satisfaction).
Focused on color and ceiling height as isolated variables, not their interaction with other environmental elements (lighting, furniture arrangement, acoustics).
Short duration of exposure to stimuli; long-term effects not studied.
Experimental design lacked cross-group comparisons of color and ceiling height.
EEG and self-reported measures could be complemented with additional physiological metrics (heart rate variability, galvanic skin response).
Reliance on VR-based simulations may lack sensory and contextual richness of real-world settings (ambient temperature, acoustics, tactile sensations absent).
Future studies should validate findings in real-world environments.
Future studies should incorporate task performance measures (learning activities, creativity tasks, learning styles, team collaboration).
minimum_safe_summary: This empirical study investigated the neurophysiological and psychological effects of color and ceiling height in virtual learning spaces on forty Korean undergraduate students. Using EEG (relative alpha power) and self-reported surveys, the study found that blue hues with high value and low chroma (HVLC) elicited the highest relaxation, while low value and high chroma (LVHC) red resulted in the least favorable outcomes. A moderate ceiling height of 4 meters provided the optimal balance for neurophysiological relaxation and psychological satisfaction, with heights exceeding this threshold diminishing comfort. While neurophysiological and psychological responses to ceiling height showed positive correlations at 4m, no significant correlations were found for color conditions, suggesting distinct processing mechanisms. Limitations include a small, homogenous sample, isolated variable focus, short exposure durations, reliance on VR, and the need for additional physiological metrics and real-world validation.
